annotations.text:
Pass 3 of 3 — desktop screens, 1440 wide.
The three office roles. Every control is a pass-1 component at its desktop values; pass 2 drew the phone.

Screens carry a dashed marker at 900: that is where a 1440×900 window stops without scrolling.

Every value shown is deliberately fake.

O2 is the screen this project turns on: it is where a garage's photographs are finally linked to a claim.

Approving is the one irreversible act in the whole product, so it waits for a visa, verifies it with NEXT3 first, and refuses outright while NEXT3 is unreachable.

Four of these five screens have no API behind them at all — only the customer link exists.

That is not a gap in the design: the broker module is later work, and these screens are its specification. Each one carries an amber note saying which part is real.

Admin is deliberately small: four CRUDs, invitations, and the failed-push queue.

The queue is the screen AXA will value most and open least. It is also unbuilt — the queue behind it runs today, and nothing surfaces it.
Nothing new was invented for the desktop. Same tokens, same banners, same chip anatomy — denser controls and one extra set of states the phone never shows.
